about.title: Where infrastructure meets human behavior
about.p1: RADIUS works where the built environment meets human behavior. Using urban informatics and data analytics, we study how complex infrastructure systems respond under stress — from cascading technical failures to how people actually behave during a disaster.
about.p2: Bridging data science and civil engineering, we build the computational frameworks for cities that are not just robust, but antifragile. We care about reach: how a single failure propagates through a network, and how a single data-driven intervention can safeguard an entire city.

pi.name: Chia-Wei Hsu
pi.bio: Chia-Wei Hsu is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at National Cheng Kung University, where he leads the RADIUS Lab. His research combines civil engineering with urban informatics and data science to study how cities — and the people in them — withstand and recover from disasters, spanning urban resilience, human mobility, disaster informatics, and infrastructure networks. He previously conducted postdoctoral research at Texas A&M University.
